why: No cam_tongue setting gets closer than 2.5 cm to the teeth, so the tip blade (0.3-5 cm, able to seal) is the only part in the catalogue that reaches the alveolar place. The tip can seal for /t/, or open to 0.05-0.15 cm2 at about 0.5-1 cm for /s/; the front cavity of about 1.5-2 cm gives a hiss near 4400-5800 Hz. For /tɑ/ the body pad can sit at its /ɑ/ posture while only the tip linkage releases, so the rail and cam servos do not turn. The body pad with stroke 1.3 also seals for /k/ and makes the /ʃ/ channel, as in proposal 1. It costs $12 (pushrod kit plus one servo), 3 days and 76 machine minutes.

No rest_area setting gets the jaw lips below 2.5 cm2 or adds any protrusion, so a different part is needed. The round lips close to 0 cm2, giving /p/ a seal with the airway open behind it. Narrowing to about 0.5-1 cm2 and protruding up to 1.6 cm lengthens the tract from 14.5 to about 16 cm and adds a constriction at the lip velocity maximum. Combined with the back tongue (F2 about 1070-1150 Hz now), that should bring F2 down to about 850-1000 Hz for /u/, /ʊ/ and /ɔ/, with F1 falling for /u/ as well. The rounding plus a tongue constriction near 3/5 of the tract also lowers F3 toward /ɝ/, which may also need the tip tongue from proposal 2. It costs $4 for the pushrod kit plus a servo ($8) if it is combined with the tip tongue, 2 days and 57 machine minutes, and it uses 6 of the 6 controller channels when combined.

Shortening the cast from 13.5 to 13.0 cm raises all formants by about 4%. The F1 ceiling goes to about 770 Hz, giving margin around 730 Hz, and the F2 reached in the high-F1 band goes to about 1020-1100 Hz, which brackets 1090 Hz. The vowel then holds under noise in a posture closer to the closure, which should help ta and possibly ka. It is a recast within the stock part's range: 40 g of silicone and 54 g of PLA, about 165 machine minutes and $0.
